findings.title: The feature-flagged table visualization receives no query results
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch passes `columns={[]}` and a `tableData` object with empty `data`, `fields`, and `units` instead of using the current `result`. Consequently, dashboard table widgets in the flagged cohort render no columns or rows even when the query returned data.

findings.title: Reports without a valid age or timestamp pass validation
findings.body: Both `age` and `timestamp` are optional, but there is no object-level check requiring exactly one, so a report containing neither is accepted and counted as valid. `age` also has no nonnegative minimum, and the mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness, allowing both fields to be present as zero. These invalid reports receive HTTP 200 and pollute the received-report metrics.

findings.title: Falsy custom cell output incorrectly falls back to the default renderer
findings.body: The renderer contract says fallback occurs when a custom renderer returns `undefined`, but this truthiness check also treats valid outputs such as `null`, `false`, `0`, and an empty string as missing. A caller cannot intentionally render a blank cell or a falsy value; the default field renderer is shown instead.

findings.title: Tabular rows cannot represent boolean field values
findings.body: `TabularValueType` includes `boolean`, but `TabularRow` only permits numbers, strings, string arrays, and null. Callers therefore cannot type valid table data for boolean fields without a cast, undermining the new table API's type safety.
